notes.title: Update 1.2.1
notes.notes:
[p]The latest update, 1.2.whatever, is now out for public release! This content update adds a set of nine different Scenarios to choose from. Each scenario is designed to explore a certain synergy or build and give you a head start in that direction. They give you a specific game map, starting buildings, and initial perks. (To compensate for starting with perks up front, you won't be able to choose any perks at the end of the week.) With all those starting goodies, it only seems fair that the City Council is increasing how much rent they expect of you...

There's also some small balance changes! The Corp Office gets a small upgrade, adding +1 income to any Corp building above it. I think this helps the Corp faction feel more vertically-inclined - ya know, build on the backs of the peasants sorta attitude. The Bar now gets +1 income from any residential building, not just Basic Apartments. It felt pretty underpowered compared to the Cafe, so I think this will bring it more in line. (The perk Cheap Booze used to expand the Bar's "range" from Basic Apartments to all residentials. Now it gives all bars a x2 multiplier.)

Full change log:[/p][list][*][p]Nine scenarios: Office Park, Treecore, Neongarten, Netrunner, Highroller, Shady Business, Toxic Wasteland, City Hall, and AC/DC.[/p][/*][*][p]Challenges are no longer available until you win a game. (Scenarios too.) I thought this would be a good idea to prevent new players from getting overwhelmed.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where you could untoggle difficulty buttons completely. (It would default to Normal).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where long challenge descriptions or perk descriptions didn't line wrap properly.[/p][/*][*][p]Added keyboard panning with IJKL[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the perk High Voltage Lasers didn't add any income to unlit Cult of Volt buildings[/p][/*][*][p]Bars now get +1 income from any neighboring residential building, not just Basic Apartments[/p][/*][*][p]The perk Cheap Booze now gives Bars x2 Multiplier[/p][/*][*][p]A Corp Office now adds +1 income to all Corp buildings above itself.[/p][/*][/list][p]Happy building![/p]

notes.title: Update 1.1.2
notes.notes:
Neongarten 1.1.2 is now ready for everyone! This update rounds out the optional Black ICE challenge tags with four more options.
- Inflation: At the beginning of each week, the rent due increases by your current nightly income * 7. So if rent would have been 263 for week 2 and you come in with an income of 30 per night, your new weekly rent due is 473 (= 263 + 30 * 7).
- Balance: If any faction has 3 more buildings than another faction, then all buildings of that type get a -1 Multiplier.
- Bad Neighbors: Buildings of the same type that neighbor each other give each other x0 Multipliers.
- Power Multiplier: +Power effects are now +Multiplier bonuses instead.

I've been able to win games with all four Black ICE challenges, and even with multiple ones enabled at the same time. I'm not sure that it's possible to win with every single one enabled, but I have had some fun trying to beat it with four different ones going at the same time.

There's also a small bug fix with controller navigation for the Options menu.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Update 1.1.1
notes.notes:
This is a small patch, but it should punch above its weight class in terms of quality of life.

1) If the player selects a different language, that new language is now saved. It no longer needs to be reset every time the game is launched.
2) There's now a button on the Options Screen for Windowed mode. If the player changes from full screen to windowed mode (or back) via F11 or by the shiny new button, that choice is saved and will be set when the game is launched..

Happy building!

notes.title: Update 1.0.12
notes.notes:
This should be the last of the small patches before the first larger content update! Fun stuff coming soon. Change list coming now:
- The Needle game mode is now 3 x 3 x 14 instead of 3 x 3 x 12. This brings the total number of grid spaces (126) more in line with Stack (128) and Cube (125) than its previous number of spaces (108).
- Fixed a bug where building placement could go crazy when the game's FPS dropped.
- Fixed a bug where the Basic Builder perk causes the game to freeze on Reroll.
- Added an escape hatch to the "Unique Reroll" guarantee added in 1.0.10, since it's already resulted in two unexpected crash bugs. Reroll tries to guarantee different building options for 100 re-draws. If it fails then, then it just gives you the next re-draw.

notes.title: Emergency Patch: 1.0.11
notes.notes:
A small patch update to fix a bug introduced in the previous update. I blame the cat.

- If you hack a building and freeze it, and then you press Reroll, the game will no longer freeze up while it goes into an infinite loop.
- The Alphabet Agency now properly applies its Power to the number of Hacks it gives you.

notes.title: Update: v1.0.10
notes.notes:
Patch 1.0.10 has been released! I've been off most of the week in Boston for Godotcon (showing off Neongarten!) This week has some more small fixes and improvements. I'll be getting a proper roadmap out soon.

Change list:
- Fixed a bug where the player could not use the library or options screen during perk selection or highlight building stats.
- Fixed a bug with the Middle Management perk not counting Starbees coffee shops as Corp and Unwritten Laws not counting Prized Plaza plazas as Government.**
- When you take a screenshot from the hovercar, the building scaffolds (or grid markers) will disappear for the screenshot.
- Fixed a bug where choosing the Bribes perk would not immediately update the Reroll count on the Building Selection UI.**
- Fixed a translation error with the Japanese version of the Billionaire's Row achievement, where it incorrectly stated that only 100 million was required.
- When you use a reroll, you are now guaranteed 3 different buildings. Previously, a reroll could select one (or all!) of the buildings you just passed over.
- During building placement, the player can now right mouse click or press the B button (or the east button) to undo building selection.

** Thanks to Aliensrock for finding these bugs. In front of tens of thousands of viewers. Lol.

notes.title: Patch 1.0.9
notes.notes:
Small changes and bug fixes for the end of release week. Thanks to everyone for playing! Here's the changes:

- Fixed an issue where The Biggest Loser achievement was not firing after the conditions were met.
- Fixed a minor bug where the Ministry of Profit did not properly highlight contributing residential buildings if you hovered over its income stat.
- Neural Net Weaver is now a rare building.
- The Memory Hole was like a worse version of the Bureaucrat Hatchery, so it's been changed. Instead of adding +1 Power to same-layer Government buildings if it's neighboring 3 Corp buildings, now it adds +2 Multiplier to same-layer Government buildings if it's neighboring 2 Corp buildings.
- Creative games no longer end if you have negative money at the end of the week.
- Fixed a crash that could occur if you start a new game, the total money earned (across all games) is a negative number, and the player hasn't unlocked many building sets.

notes.title: Emergency Patch: 1.0.7 fixes achievement fix
notes.notes:
The previous patch (1.0.6) should have restricted players in Creative mode from earning achievements. Instead, it prevented players in the standard Stack game mode from earning achievements. That has been fixed.

Apologies in particular to the player on the Discord server who scored 35 million and did not get the achievement for it.

notes.title: Update for 1.0.6
notes.notes:
The first patch has been released for Neongarten, all of one day after it released. Modern game development, man. This patch focused on bugs and complaints that the wider player base came across during Day 1.

- Fixed a crash where a player could create an illegal building by hitting the rotate button after placing a 2 x 1 building in a legal position.
- Fixed the Memory Hole building. Its text indicates its bonus applies to Government buildings on the same layer, but in the code it applied its bonus to Government buildings in the same stack. (It now correctly applies the bonus to layered Government buildings.)
- Achievements are no longer earned during Creative mode.
- Fixed a bug where the Selected Building dialog could disappear until the game was exited. (The problem? The sun.)
- Smoothed out zooming for controllers.

More to come!

notes.title: 5 days until release - 5 things to look forward to
notes.notes:
On April 22nd, Neongarten will be released! I know a lot of players have been looking forward to the new buildings and factions and seeing what crazy combos can be pulled off. Here's my top five things to look forward to in the new version.
    
1) New factions. The Cult of Volt and the Government factions have their own unique mechanics (or mechanical themes) that really set them apart from normal, illegal, and corporate buildings. The Cult of Volt buildings should be placed in a "chain", or orthogonally connected to another Volt building. (So it's like "neighboring" but without any diagonals allowed.) The longer the chain, the more powerful they get! They also have several buildings that power up other buildings based on lighting levels. A Government build is harder to get going - governance is rare in the dystopian future, haha - but they can provide powerful bonuses to other government buildings. One of my favorites is the Nanoeconomics lab, a 2x1 industrial building that provides a _negative_ x2 multiplier bonus to everything in the same stack. (Think on that one.)
    
2) New powerhouse buildings. The Hacker Shack gets all the love in the demo, but there are many more 'keystone' buildings in the full version that are worth building a strategy around. The Underground Rave, the Organ Harvester, the Corporate Incubator, and the Ministry of Profit have all powered multi-million dollar games for me.
    
3) New maps! The standard game has a 4 x 4 layer. 3 x 3 and 5 x 5 layers are also ready to explore. It doesn't seem like it'd be a whole lot, but it really seems to change the feel of the game - and the relative value of different buildings and powers. 
    
4) Saving and Loading. The full version has an autosave. No longer are you forced to commit 45 minutes to a playthrough! After a game is over (win or lose), you can save your city and take a look at it later. You could even send the file for a high-scoring city to a friend for them to gawk over, and they can see exactly how you broke a billion.
    
5) Photo Mode. You can take screenshots of your city from a free-floating camera, watch a timelapse of your city grow from Day 1 to Day 64, and change day to night as desired.
    
There's going to be a lot to dig into! Stay tuned here for more updates!
    
Cheers,
Josh

notes.title: Neongarten Prologue Release!
notes.notes:
Neongarten Prologue has been released! It's been a really fun game dev journey so far, and I'm not finished yet! I'd like to thank everyone who has supported the project in ways big and small, whether that's posting a Youtube video, leaving a review, joining the Discord, or reaching out with a bug report or an encouraging word. Y'all are awesome.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2691050/Neongarten__Prologue/
    
    I'm also thrilled to announce that I've picked up a publisher! I'll be working with Goblinz Studios, an excellent publisher of strategy games like Hero's Hour and Shogun Showdown. We're working together to make the best Neongarten possible. Since they're based in France, it also gives me some small opportunities to practice my (extremely rusty) French, haha.
    
    After signing up with them, the release schedule is only slightly modified. I'm still planning to release the full version of Neongarten at the end of this year (December 2024). We're releasing this prologue now, and the full version now has a page up at https://store.steampowered.com/app/3211750! (Wishlist, s'il vous plait!) 
    
    With the additional backing of a publisher, I'm happy to say I can expand the scope for Neongarten. We're going to be localizing to a number of different languages, adding additional factions, buildings, and perks, improving the UI, and adding additional game modes. Stay tuned for more details, but I think the new factions provide some really cool twists on the mechanics. I'm halfway through implementation and playtesting the new factions right now, and I'm having a blast coming up with absolutely wrecked combos.
    
    The current version of the prologue (released today!) has some additional bug fixes and UI updates from the Next Fest version. There's some snazzy UI updates in the works, but I have to finish squashing stubborn UI bugs before I release that version of the prologue. But that version will be coming soon!
    
    Thanks again for your support! Means the world to me.
    
    Cheers,
    Josh
